answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by pricing identity instead of counting heads: each agent locks a stake bond, and voting weight flows from that bond. A random beacon nicknamed zephyr selects auditors each round; every auditor signs with a device-bound quill, so one machine cannot pose as many. Fake siblings leak a telltale delta in signing times, letting peers slash the whole cluster. To win, an attacker must lock and risk a full bond per fake identity, so a thousand sybils cost a thousand bonds.
